name: Track promises people make you and chase them before they go cold with Gmail, Google Sheets and OpenAI

parameters.content:
# START HERE — 4 steps

**Step 1** · Attach credentials: Gmail, Google Sheets, OpenAI (3 total).

**Step 2** · Press play on the orange **SETUP** trigger (Lane D, bottom). It creates your ledger spreadsheet — two tabs, headers, example rows — and prints a `spreadsheet_id`.

**Step 3** · Create a Gmail label `promises-processed`, copy its label ID. Open **Workflow Config** — paste `spreadsheet_id`, `label_id`, and your `owner_email`. One node; everything reads it.

**Step 4** · Delete Lane D, set the workflow **Active**. Hourly scans find promises in your inbox; at 08:00 (workflow timezone) the sweep drafts chases into `Chase-Queue` for your approval.

_Preview first? Press **Test workflow** — the demo lane runs six emails offline._

## Promise ledger — remember what people owe you, chase it before it goes cold

**Who it's for:** founders and operators who lose follow-ups in their inbox — vendors who "will send it Friday", partners who owe a document, clients who promised a reply.

**How it works:** hourly, the inbox is scanned and an AI extracts concrete promises {who, what, due-by}. Each lands in the `Commitments` ledger (deduped on person+promise). At 08:00 the sweep classifies open rows — due today, overdue, 3+ days overdue — and drafts a polite chase email into `Chase-Queue`. You approve the draft, it goes out; the ledger row moves open→reminded→chased→escalated. When the person finally delivers, the intake marks the row `done` and it drops out of your digest.

**The approval gate:** nothing is ever sent automatically — chase drafts wait for your go-ahead, so the automation can never embarrass you with a wrong chase.

**Morning digest:** a daily email groups open promises by person with age — you see at a glance who habitually leaves commitments hanging.

**Setup:** 3 credentials, one button, one paste — see START HERE.

### Lane A — inbox intake (runs every hour except 08:00)

Gmail poll → decode raw MIME → AI extracts promises per message (strict JSON) → parse → route: new commitment → ledger appendOrUpdate on `dedupe_key`; fulfillment reply → oldest open row for that person marked `done`; vague/low-confidence → review alert (emailed); not a promise → skip.

Processed messages get the `promises-processed` label so they never rescan.

### Lane B — daily chase sweep (08:00 workflow timezone)

Read ledger → classify due-today / overdue / >=3d → AI drafts the chase → `Chase-Queue` (pending-approval) + owner notification → the row is marked reminded/chased; >=3d escalates straight to you and is marked `escalated` so it fires once.

One digest email per run: due/overdue/escalated counts + aging by person.

### Lane C — demo (no credentials)

"Test workflow" fires six emails: a clear promise, a vague one (no date), a fulfillment reply, a duplicate, a non-promise, and a simulated bad AI answer — every route runs offline.

Delete the demo lane when live.

### ⚠ Approval before send

Chase drafts land in `Chase-Queue` with `pending-approval`. To send one: copy the draft to a Gmail compose (or wire a send node of your own). The workflow deliberately never sends on your behalf.

### Lane D — first-run setup (run once)

Attach a Google Sheets credential, press play on the orange trigger. Creates `Commitments` + `Chase-Queue` tabs with headers and done-marked example rows, prints the `spreadsheet_id` — paste into **Workflow Config**, delete this lane.

nodes.notes: Exactly one per run — fed by a single wave so branch shape can never multiply it.

nodes.name: Extract promises (AI)
nodes.notes: Strict-JSON verdict per message: has_promise, promise, due_date, confidence, closes_previous.

nodes.name: Merge write streams
nodes.notes: New commitments and fulfillment closures share one credential gate.

nodes.name: Live write?
nodes.notes: Demo items skip real writes; production items write the ledger and label the email.

nodes.name: Write kind?
nodes.notes: fulfillment → close the matching open row; everything else (commitment) → upsert the ledger.

nodes.name: Write ledger row
nodes.notes: appendOrUpdate on dedupe_key (person+promise hash) — repeats update the row, never duplicate it. continueErrorOutput: a failed write must NOT reach the label — the unlabelled message retries next hour.

nodes.name: Find open row
nodes.notes: Reads the ledger so the fulfillment can close the right row.

nodes.name: Pick open row
nodes.notes: Closes the OLDEST open row for closes_person; emits nothing when nothing is open.

nodes.name: Row matched?
nodes.notes: Matched → close the ledger row; unmatched fulfillment → label anyway so it is not re-scanned every hour.

nodes.name: Mark done in ledger
nodes.notes: update semantics — closes the row without touching promise/due_date/confidence. continueErrorOutput: no label without a written ledger row.

nodes.name: Label email processed
nodes.notes: Label ID (not name) from Workflow Config. Applied AFTER the ledger write — a failed run re-scans instead of losing the message.

nodes.name: Skip is live?
nodes.notes: Not-a-promise mail is labelled too (otherwise it is re-fetched and re-sent to the AI every hour for a day). Demo items stop here.

nodes.name: Alert is live?
nodes.notes: Demo alerts stop here; live alerts email the owner.

nodes.name: Read ledger rows
nodes.notes: Reads every row — the classifier owns the status filter (open/reminded/chased are active) because a single-column equality can't express the active set.

nodes.name: Sweep digest
nodes.notes: One digest per sweep — fed directly by the classifier wave.

nodes.name: Digest worth sending?
nodes.notes: Skip the morning email when nothing is due, overdue, escalated or flagged.

parameters.content:
### Error lane — instance-level catch-all

This workflow carries an `Error Trigger` entry point: point **Settings → Error workflow** of this workflow (or any sibling) at it, and every unhandled failure is formatted and emailed to the owner. The owner address is a literal in `Format error alert` — Workflow Config never runs inside an error-triggered execution.

**Inert until wired:** exports cannot carry `settings.errorWorkflow`, so attach it once after import.

**Contract** — side_effects: one Gmail send per failed execution. rollback: detach the error workflow in Settings.

nodes.name: On workflow error
nodes.notes: Attach this workflow as the error workflow (Settings → Error workflow) so any unhandled failure emails the owner.

nodes.name: Format error alert
nodes.notes: One item per failed execution — names the workflow, node and execution link.

nodes.name: Email owner: promise-ledger error
nodes.notes: Only fires inside an error-triggered execution — never in the demo lane.
